blockers.quote: What if you could see who wants you to fail?
blockers.why: Check #3 / #15 fails: the draft places the premise question around 0:36, after the required 0:30 second hook.
blockers.fix: Replace lines 36–38 with: “That card opens when you say good news. What if it shows who wants you to fail? The next face is your best friend.” Then cut this repeated line.

suggestions.quote: Sixty seconds. The card folds shut. His arm stays. So does the number.
suggestions.fix: Keep the -84 card visible until sixty actual story seconds after line 45, then fold it during the rule scene; the current timestamps give it roughly twenty seconds.

suggestions.quote: You take your bag. And you don't go home. Not that night. Not for a month.
suggestions.fix: Replace with: “You take your bag. And you don't go home that night. For the next month, you don't say good news to her face.” This preserves the month-long silence without conflicting with the following one-week study-room sequence.

suggestions.quote: At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver (c08). Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing (c08).
suggestions.fix: Cut this post-peak comparison; her hidden letter already reveals the life she nearly had, and the statistic delays that personal landing.

keep.quote: You stopped helping him. He never stopped helping you.
The card gets two minutes. It doesn't get to choose what you do next.
That half-second is the other life, going past.
